app-regressions:R2-1.title: A pending recording is deleted on the next launch if PC Clipper ends without running the engine's rescue
app-regressions:R2-1.problem: Pending recordings are held only in memory (ReplayEngine Session.PendingRecordings). The KEEP marker that protects their session folder is written only at the end of TearDownSessionAsync -> RescuePendingRecordingsAsync (ReplayEngine.cs 751-754). On every launch, StartupAsync -> CleanupStaleBufferAsync calls SegmentStore.CleanupStaleSessions(root, null), and so does the engine's StartAsync for a new session. Both delete every session folder that has no marker. So if the process ends any other way while a recording is pending, the footage is deleted at the next start: a crash, power loss, a forced Windows Update restart, 'Shut down anyway' while ExitAsync is still retrying, Task Manager End task, or 'Close anyway' during step 3/4. That breaks the SPEC promise 'Recordings are never thrown away by a failed save'.
app-regressions:R2-1.scenario: A 45-minute recording can't be saved because the clips drive is full. The banner says 'PC Clipper is keeping it until it can be saved.' The user leaves the PC, and Windows Update force-restarts it overnight (or the user clicks 'Shut down anyway' on the blocked-shutdown screen while ExitAsync retries the copy). PC Clipper is killed before RescuePendingRecordingsAsync writes 'KEEP - unsaved recording.txt'. With Start with Windows on, the next launch runs CleanupStaleBufferAsync, which deletes session_* along with the 45 minutes of segments. No message is shown.
app-regressions:R2-1.verified_fix: In ReplayEngine.SaveRecordingAsync's finally, when the recording is added back to s.PendingRecordings, also write SegmentStore.KeepMarkerName (best effort) into s.Dir. Ideally include a small manifest: run numbers, StartRun signature, StartIndex and StartedLocal, so the recording can be re-saved later. When PendingRecordings becomes empty after a successful save, delete the marker. TearDownSessionAsync still deletes the folder when !KeepFolder, so normal stops are unchanged. Pair this with R2-5's start-up scan so a marked folder is reported to the user rather than only being skipped.

app-regressions:R2-2.title: PC Clipper quits and deletes the buffer on WM_QUERYENDSESSION, even if the shutdown is then cancelled
app-regressions:R2-2.problem: OnWindowsShutdown always fires ExitAsync(sessionEnding: true). It is called from MainForm.OnFormClosing for WindowsShutDown/TaskManagerClosing (MainForm.cs 303-304) and from OnSessionEnding (line 2377), and both run when WM_QUERYENDSESSION arrives. That message is only a query: another app can still veto it, or the user can press Cancel on Windows' 'apps are preventing shutdown' screen, and Windows then sends WM_ENDSESSION(FALSE). When nothing needs protecting, PC Clipper has already answered TRUE and started ExitAsync, so it stops the engine (TearDownSessionAsync deletes the session folder) and calls ExitThread whatever the outcome. The round-1 change creates the hidden window's handle at start-up, so MainForm now always takes this path, also for minimized/tray starts.
app-regressions:R2-2.scenario: The replay buffer is on with 15 minutes buffered and nothing is being saved. The user clicks Restart, Notepad (unsaved file) blocks the shutdown, and the user presses Cancel. PC Clipper has already stopped capture, deleted the buffer and removed its tray icon. The gameplay the user meant to clip is gone, and the replay stays off until they relaunch the app. The same happens when someone runs 'shutdown /a', or when an app's WM_QUERYENDSESSION handler vetoes the shutdown.
app-regressions:R2-2.verified_fix: On the query (MainForm.OnFormClosing WindowsShutDown and OnSessionEnding), only decide: if ShouldBlockShutdown, set e.Cancel = true, call BlockShutdown() and finish the pending saves (existing ExitAsync path, or a save-only wait). Otherwise set e.Cancel = false and do nothing else. Override MainForm.WndProc for WM_ENDSESSION (0x0016), or subscribe SystemEvents.SessionEnded, which fires only when wParam != 0. On TRUE, do a synchronous best-effort stop (_engine.StopAsync() waited up to ~3 s), then Shutdown(). On FALSE, call AllowShutdown() (ShutdownBlockReasonDestroy) and keep running. If saves were being finished for a blocked shutdown, cancel the pending exit once they complete, or set _exiting only on ENDSESSION(TRUE).

app-regressions:R2-3.title: Turn ON / Try again after a replay fault silently reuses the old capture format and ignores changed settings
app-regressions:R2-3.problem: From the Problem state (engine Faulted, _wantReplayOn false), StartReplayAsync(User) passes keepBuffer = true. The engine then reuses the faulted session and calls KeepBufferFormat (the round-1 resume fix). Whenever the new config's Signature differs, KeepBufferFormat forces the previous run's Width, Height, Fps, BitrateKbps, Vendor, Codec and EncoderName. ApplySettingsAsync treats this state as not active (ReplayWanted is false), so a capture-settings change neither restarts nor clears the faulted session. Problem state offers only 'Turn ON' (ToggleReplay computes on = false), so the user has no way to get a fresh format short of restarting the app or changing the buffer folder.
app-regressions:R2-3.scenario: The replay stops with 'Drive C: is almost full ..., so the replay buffer was stopped. Free up space or pick another drive in Settings.' The user lowers Resolution from Native 4K to 1080p and Quality to Medium, presses Save ('Settings saved.'), then presses Try again. The new run starts at 3840x2160 at the old bitrate (Home shows 'HEVC (NVIDIA) - 3840x2160 - 60 fps - ...'), fills the disk at the same rate and stops again. The same happens when the user follows 'Lower the resolution or frame rate' or 'pick another encoder in Settings' after a non-retryable resume failure: the same failing format is used again.
app-regressions:R2-3.verified_fix: Apply KeepBufferFormat only to supervised resumes. Add a flag to the engine, e.g. StartAsync(cfg, keepBuffer, keepFormat), and pass keepFormat: kind == StartKind.Resume. In StartReplayAsync for a User/Hotkey start from Faulted, set keepBuffer = _engine.ActiveConfig is null || BuildConfig(...).Signature == _engine.ActiveConfig.Signature. When they differ, start fresh (keepBuffer: false), confirming first if footage is buffered or a recording is pending. The engine's !keepBuffer path already runs FinishRecordingIfAny plus TearDown and Rescue. Alternatively or additionally, in ApplySettingsAsync, when captureChanged && !active && _engine.State == Faulted, stop that session after the same confirm, so the next start is fresh.

app-regressions:R2-4.title: During 'Try again' the pending count is 0: banner and tray item vanish, and the unsaved-recording warnings are skipped
app-regressions:R2-4.problem: ReplayEngine.RetryPendingRecordingsAsync clears Session.PendingRecordings before it saves (ReplayEngine.cs 665-669) and adds a recording back only if its save fails. During the whole retry, SafePendingRecordings() is 0. RecordingBannerText therefore returns null instead of the intended 'Saving your recording again...' (that branch is dead after the first refresh). The tray item 'Save the unsaved recording again' hides, and the guards that rely on the count are bypassed: ToggleReplay's 'A recording isn't saved yet' confirm (line 438), TestPcAsync's 'A recording still needs saving' gate (line 1971), and the pending note in ApplySettingsAsync's confirm (line 1886).
app-regressions:R2-4.scenario: A long pending recording is retried. The concat runs for minutes, and the banner disappears right away as if the recording were saved. The user presses Turn OFF and gets no warning. If the retry then fails (the drive fills mid-copy, a USB drive is unplugged), StopReplayAsync -> StopAsync -> RescuePendingRecordingsAsync fails too. The recording is left as raw segments that 'can't be saved as a video from there', which is exactly what the skipped dialog would have warned about.
app-regressions:R2-4.verified_fix: In AppController, record int _retryingCount = SafePendingRecordings() just before calling the engine, and clear it in the finally. Have PendingRecordingCount and RecordingBannerIsPending use Math.Max(_retryingCount, engine count) while _retryingRecordings is true, and use that same helper in the ToggleReplay, TestPcAsync and ApplySettingsAsync checks. Better: in ReplayEngine, keep each recording in PendingRecordings (marked InProgress) until its save succeeds, and remove it only on success, so PendingRecordingCount is never transiently 0.

app-regressions:R2-5.title: A recording kept as raw video at exit or shutdown is never reported, then or on later launches
app-regressions:R2-5.problem: When the final rescue in StopAsync fails, the engine keeps the session folder and raises 'A recording couldn't be saved. Its raw video was kept in <dir>.' OnEngineNotice stores this in _keptRecordingNotice (memory only) and returns before notifying when _exiting is set, which is always the case on the exit and Windows-shutdown paths (ExitAsync steps 3 and 4). On the next launch, CleanupStaleBufferAsync/CleanupStaleSessions skip folders that have the KEEP marker, but nothing lists or reports them. Windows shutdown shows no confirmation dialog either, unlike ExitApp.
app-regressions:R2-5.scenario: A pending recording exists because the clips drive is full, and the user shuts Windows down. PC Clipper holds the shutdown, retries twice (both fail on the free-space check), keeps the folder and exits without a word. After the reboot, PC Clipper shows no banner. Tens of GB of raw footage sit unseen in %LOCALAPPDATA%\PCClipper\Buffer\session_..., the user believes the recording is lost, and the space is never reclaimed.
app-regressions:R2-5.verified_fix: In StartupAsync, after CleanupStaleBufferAsync, enumerate BufferFolder for session_* dirs that contain SegmentStore.KeepMarkerName. Set _keptRecordingNotice to e.g. 'A recording that couldn't be saved earlier was kept in <dir>.' with the existing Open folder button, and add a Delete action that removes the folder after a confirm. With R2-1's manifest, offer 'Save it now' too. On the exit and shutdown path, log the kept path and, when the tray still exists, show a balloon before Shutdown(); the next-launch banner covers the shutdown case.

app-regressions:R2-6.title: Record/save debounce uses the wall clock: a backwards clock step silently swallows the Stop press
app-regressions:R2-6.problem: The round-1 debounce compares DateTime.UtcNow with _lastRecordToggleUtc (line 1613) and with _lastSaveRequestUtc (line 1555). If the system clock steps backwards (time sync after resume from sleep, a manual time change), now - last becomes negative, which is always below the 600 ms or 1 s limit. Every press is then ignored, with only a log line and no toast or sound, until the wall clock passes the stored value again. Rejected presses (for example while 'Replay is still starting') also re-arm the save debounce.
app-regressions:R2-6.scenario: The user starts recording with the hotkey. While they play, Windows time sync corrects a clock that was running 5 minutes fast. When they press the Record hotkey to stop, nothing happens, and keeps not happening for about 5 minutes. They believe the recording stopped and saved, but it is still running.
app-regressions:R2-6.verified_fix: Store Environment.TickCount64 (or Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()) instead of DateTime.UtcNow in _lastRecordToggleUtc and _lastSaveRequestUtc, and compare elapsed milliseconds: long now = Environment.TickCount64; if (now - last < 600) ignore. In SaveLastAsync, set the timestamp only after the CanSave and folder checks pass, i.e. when a save is actually started. Optionally, use the same monotonic clock for the engine's stall watchdog (JanitorTick's DateTime.UtcNow - lastNew), where a forward step falsely triggers 'Screen capture froze'.

fix-completeness:R1-core-concurrency:F4/.title: Keeping the buffer format overrides the user's changed settings when replay is restarted from a Faulted state
fix-completeness:R1-core-concurrency:F4/.problem: StartAsync calls KeepBufferFormat on every keepBuffer start that has a session. It replaces Width/Height/Fps/BitrateKbps/Vendor/Codec/EncoderName with those of session.Current. The round-1 fix was meant only for supervised resumes "and the user's capture settings have not changed". AppController.StartReplayAsync passes keepBuffer=true for any non-Restart start while the engine is Faulted (AppController.cs:1032), which covers the banner's "Try again" and "Turn ON". ApplySettingsAsync restarts (and so tears the session down) only when `captureChanged && active` (AppController.cs:1929). After a non-retryable fault, ReplayWanted is false, so changed capture settings are saved but the old session survives, and the next start silently restores the old format.
fix-completeness:R1-core-concurrency:F4/.scenario: The replay stops with a non-retryable fault such as "Drive C: is almost full ... replay buffer was stopped", or a failed resume such as "Your graphics card's encoder can't handle these settings ... Lower the resolution or frame rate, or switch codec in Settings" or "...pick the encoder of the GPU this screen is plugged into". The user follows the advice: they lower Quality/Resolution or pick another encoder, click Apply (no restart prompt, because the replay is not active), and press Try again. KeepBufferFormat puts back the old bitrate, size and encoder, so the drive fills again or the same encoder error repeats. Every later Turn ON does the same, because the Faulted session is never torn down. The user is stuck until they change the buffer folder or restart PC Clipper. Changing the monitor while Faulted likewise records the new monitor scaled into the old monitor's size.
fix-completeness:R1-core-concurrency:F4/.verified_fix: Separate 'continue the buffer' from 'keep its format'. Give StartAsync an explicit `keepFormat` parameter and call KeepBufferFormat only when it is true. In AppController, set keepFormat = (kind == StartKind.Resume) || (Faulted && the capture settings have not changed since the session started). For the second check, keep a snapshot of the AppSettings used for the session's last successful start and compare it with CaptureDiffers. When the settings did change, start with keepFormat=false. The old incompatible runs then drop out exactly as after any settings change, or the App can pass keepBuffer:false, which tears down via FinishRecordingIfAnyAsync and TearDownSessionAsync (pending recordings are rescued there). A simpler alternative: in ApplySettingsAsync, when captureChanged && !active && _engine.State == Faulted, call StopReplayAsync(announce:false). It already retries pending recordings and waits for saves before StopAsync.
